newsitem.title: USA: Record U.S. cigarette production seen in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Record U.S. cigarette production seen in 1996.

text.p: U.S. tobacco companies will manufacture a record number of cigarettes this year, largely to meet burgeoning overseas demand, the government said Monday.
The Agriculture Department estimated U.S. cigarette production would climb to 760 billion cigarettes in 1996, the highest on record, and up from roughly 747 billion cigarettes made the prior year.
Americans smoked about 487 billion cigarettes in 1996, the department said. Consumption has remained about the same for the past four years.

However, U.S. cigarette exports grew by 12.5 percent to 260 billion in 1996. Exports have been trending upwards strongly since the mid-1980s. By comparison, in 1985 U.S. cigarette exports rang in at 58.9 billion.

Department analyst Tom Capehart said increased sales to Pacific Rim countries, Asia and Europe, high quality cigarettes and more efficient manufacturing were the main reasons for the gain. He also cited efforts by the tobacco industry to find new markets abroad as interest waned at home.

The tobacco industry faces massive legal fights on numerous fronts. Eighteen state attorneys general, New York City, and the California cities of San Francisco and San Jose and counties including Los Angeles have sued the industry to recoup health care costs of smokers.
The U.S. tobacco crop is forecast at 1.55 billion pounds in 1996, up 22 percent from the prior year.
Cigar consumption is expected to climb 16 percent and snuff consumption may also rise, but chewing and smoking tobacco use continues to decline, the department said.
